workflowChanges: Review each real application afresh: prior character consensus establishes source continuity, not profile approval or an automatic score.
Separate portable identity from host layout. Carry character version, palette, name mapping, voice and factual project names forward; let GitHub and the website use their appropriate layouts.

Compare the sidebar bio and README together on desktop, then separately in mobile reading order. Repetition can help orientation on mobile while still costing specificity in the combined desktop view.
Maintain a public-copy boundary: private work may be acknowledged at the owner's stated level; only owner-cleared stories and evidence become future public website material.
Use viewport captures for identity/header visibility and full-page captures for lower content. Record inconsistent sticky/capture state instead of turning it into a fabricated product defect.
Keep a public-project facts record for names, scope and maturity; future website elaboration must agree with GitHub wording and may add verified decisions rather than broader unsupported claims.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason: Native GitHub owns typography, spacing, controls and responsive layout. Taste-skill custom CSS, section-per-screen, full-screen heroes, font pairing, layout dealers and checker recipes are not requirements for this application.

The taste-skill ban on greetings in a commercial hero does not override this personal profile's useful 'Hey, I'm Nag' attribution. The owner supplied the established name; no new brand-name search or coining is needed.
Mandatory photographs, real-product frames, shaders, hover loops and button-motion layers do not fit this static GitHub-native introduction. Their absence is not a defect.
No commercial hard number, price, customer logo or testimonial should be invented to satisfy a first-screen proof recipe. Real public repository links provide appropriate evidence here.
The local-preview banner is review provenance, not final profile copy. The skill's no-placeholder/sample-note rule does not justify removing that evidence label.
No skills authorize publication, private-work disclosure, a new website build or browser operation by this reviewer.
UI animation timing and GPU advice do not apply to these static PNGs; future website behavior remains purposeful and optional under the existing character contract.
scoreMeaning: Out of 10 for the current prepared GitHub application's brand craft: a coherent, legible and honestly attributed personal introduction with useful public destinations. Held below exceptional because the introductory voice repeats broad maker qualities more than it conveys a distinctive specific approach. This is a fresh application score, not a numerical continuation of the 8.6 gesture-foundation score, website approval or human recognition evidence.
confidence: High for inspected static coherence, attribution and source/application consistency; moderate for editorial distinctiveness judgment. No confidence claim for unseen human outcomes, physical-device behavior or live account settings.
strengths: The full personal name, heyNag handle, large wordmark and first-person Nag heading clearly assign authorship to a person. The moth does not speak in place of him.
Avatar and header share the same soft head, unequal paddles and cream/green vocabulary; the header restores the full winged silhouette. Both light and dark previews remain visibly the same identity.
The paper-ground day avatar remains useful in the dark GitHub shell. It gives the face a stable boundary instead of forcing the weaker small night antenna treatment into the universal account slot.
Charms, Grok Bot and eva.md are concrete public destinations with concise descriptions. Grok Bot is explicitly unofficial and eva.md remains an evolving experiment, avoiding inflated outcomes.
The private-work sentence explains the limited public sample without naming, linking or describing private projects. It avoids treating this profile as the whole of Nag's work.

The page uses live native text for the introduction and projects; the image supplies identity. At 320px the wordmark is readable and none of the project meaning depends on decoding a tiny mitten or antenna.
The website field is deliberately empty while heyNag.com is unfinished. The continuity contract calls for a reciprocal link only when a useful destination exists.

The continuity plan preserves stable assets/name/voice while allowing the future website to add verified decisions and optional Investigate & share behavior. Static GitHub use is a valid part of that system.

deductions.finding: The bio and README opening repeat nearly the same cluster: software/systems, useful tools, curiosity and how software feels. In the combined desktop view, the second introduction adds little particular knowledge of Nag.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Keep the concise mobile-useful bio, but let the README's next sentence eventually contribute one owner-verified way of working, current question or specific observation instead of restating the same qualities. Do not invent an anecdote, seniority or result.

deductions.kind: current degree of distinctiveness, not a scope blocker
evidence: README.md project descriptions and closing line
deductions.finding: Most personal specificity comes from the character and the choice of three projects. The descriptions clearly say what they do, but they give only a small glimpse of Nag's own decisions; the warm closing line remains broadly reusable.
deductions.improvementCriterion: When an appropriate public detail is available, add one concise truthful author-specific detail to this introduction or the linked project destination. Reserve richer authorized stories for the website. A GitHub profile does not need a full case study, and no private material is required.

recommendations: Accept this as a prepared local GitHub application with the existing header/avatar identity and three public destinations; publication remains a separate action under the user's actual authorization.
Keep the clear first-person attribution and private-work boundary. Do not replace it with mascot dialogue, fabricated impact or public hints about undisclosed work.
Preserve source/version links across static exports and future website character use. Reuse the identity, not necessarily the GitHub banner's exact layout as the website hero.

At website implementation time, demonstrate the shared wordmark/character/voice and reciprocal public project links in actual screenshots. Add heyNag.com to GitHub only when its destination is useful and live.
Treat deeper author-specific proof as a future content opportunity; do not reopen tiny anatomy or add motion to solve generic prose.

continuityAssessment.currentDemonstrated: The local GitHub preview consistently connects Nagarjuna Boddu, heyNag and Nag to the same moth and public project sample. The static identity works without access to the signature's motion.
continuityAssessment.planSupported: continuity.json is a coherent contract for the same character version, tokens, first-person authorship, public project names and honest maturity on the future website. It appropriately reserves deeper stories and optional character behavior for that surface.
continuityAssessment.notDemonstrated: No website implementation or side-by-side website/GitHub experience exists in this review. The plan's recognition language is a design intention, not measured transfer, memory or attribution.
continuityAssessment.privacy: Only the user's broad private-work acknowledgment appears in public copy. No private project names, screenshots, code, internal links or inferred achievements were introduced.
continuityAssessment.captureCaveat: Full 320px captures show a blank name/handle region and a sticky navigation strip over part of the banner. Root supplied actual top and wheel-scrolled viewport captures; I inspected all five. These confirm visible name/handle/header at the top, complete readable project copy while scrolling, and all three pins. The earlier full-page inconsistency is treated as capture state, not an application defect; use the viewport evidence for final claims.
